smbd_deltas: confirmed per mariowiki: smbd replaces the nes warp-zone room's 3-pipe world-select with a room containing brick blocks, three ? blocks, 22 coins, and a power-up brick block - i.e. smbd 1-2 likely has no functional warp zone / world skip in this spot, or it is relocated elsewhere (not found in sources used). the warp_zone area entry and warps[] array above describe the measured NES layout; do not assume they apply unmodified to smbd until the gbc map is pixel-measured the same way. total coin count also differs: 68 coins (nes) vs 90 coins (smbd challenge mode) per mariowiki, implying additional coins were added somewhere in the smbd layout beyond just the warp-zone-room replacement.
confidence_notes: this pass fixes the fidelity gap the previous one knowingly shipped: 1-2 began directly underground with no above-ground start and its ending was appended as more columns of the same underground-typed grid, so the flagpole and castle stood under a cave ceiling. the engine still models a level as one typed grid plus pipe-triggered sub-areas that return to their entry point, which cannot express "overworld, then underground, then overworld again" on its own - so this pass extends the bible/compiler with the smaller of the two options considered: a `segments` list of column ranges, each with its own type, layered on top of the level's single base type (compile_level.py's compiled_segments()/type_at()/first_row_at()). apply_ceiling() now stamps the roof only inside underground-typed ranges when segments are present, and the roof-dependent row skip (piranha pipe caps, start/jump landing rows) is now looked up per column instead of once for the whole level. the palette equivalent lives at runtime: level_palette_set() takes the current camera column and consults the same segment table (empty on every level but 1-2), and terrain.c's new terrain_sync_palette() re-loads the bg palette set whenever that answer can have changed - once at every terrain_init() and again after any same-grid jump. the three ranges are walled off from each other with a full-height 'elevation' block at each seam (columns 24 and 216) so a player cannot simply walk from one into the next; the only crossing is a new terrain kind on a pipe, `jump_to`, compiled to a new object kind (kObjPipeJump) and a small jump_target_column/row table on LevelInfo - pressing down over one of these cuts to the target column with the lcd off (main.c's jump_to_segment(), mirroring the existing enter_sub_area()/leave_sub_area() pattern) without any level_load, because level_grid already holds the whole level (every segment) at once; only the vram ring and the bg palette catch up. a second new terrain kind, `castle`, places a decorative castle (apply_castle with no flag beside it) for the start segment's own castle. rejected alternative: a real area graph where a sub-area's exit could target another named area instead of always returning to the entry point - more faithful and more reusable for a future world 2, but it would touch blocks.c/enemies.c's per-area state reset and the flagpole/end-of-level logic that only reads the main level's own fields today; not worth it for one level's fix. capacity impact: length_columns grows 224 -> 258 (+34 columns), which becomes the new LEVEL_GRID_COLUMNS (the WRAM level_grid ring is sized to the longest level or widest sub-area, whichever is bigger) - +34*16 = 544 bytes of WRAM. LEVEL_MAX_OBJECTS grows by the two new kObjPipeJump entries this level adds (self-adjusting, gen_levels.py already takes the max across levels). the compiled grid array itself grows the same 544 bytes in 1-2's own rom bank (bank 2), comfortably inside a 16kb bank. two judgement calls worth flagging: (1) the underground run's own exit pipe column (166 in the old, pre-rebuild coordinate space) is not clearly distinguishable from the warp-zone room's approach in the map rip, so its exact column is a compiler choice, not a measurement - placed just past the lift shaft and before the warp-zone corridor, which is the right neighborhood per mariowiki's prose description of the route; (2) both segment transitions (down the entrance pipe, down the exit pipe) play the same 'sink then cut' beat main.c already uses for entering a sub-area, rather than a 'rise up out of a pipe' beat on arrival (which the real game's exit pipe does) - reusing the engine's own existing arrival convention (enter_sub_area never plays an arrival animation either) rather than adding a second one. neither takes away from the acceptance test: mario starts under open sky with the castle behind him, goes down a real pipe to reach the cave, and the flagpole/castle at the end have sky above them, not rock.
